# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm the Blind monkey. I received a spoken message, but wait - Deaf cannot speak (Deaf can only gesture, since Deaf cannot hear/touch but can see). Let me reconsider - actually the message says "Deaf says" which seems inconsistent with the rules... but I should just work with what I'm given as my perceived input.

Actually, re-reading rules: Deaf can see but not hear or speak? Let me check - the rules don't explicitly forbid Deaf from speaking, only from hearing/touching. So Deaf CAN speak. That makes sense - Deaf speaks to Mute (who can hear), and gestures to Blind... wait no, Blind cannot see gestures either.

Wait, I need to re-check my channels: "When you speak, Mute receives it. When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." This is about MY channels. For Deaf: Deaf can speak (voice) which Mute would hear, and gesture which... only sighted people receive gestures, but Blind cannot see. So Deaf's speech goes to Mute only (I'm Blind, I can't hear either since I "cannot see a color, gesture or anything merely printed" - wait, can I hear?

Blind's restriction: "Cannot: See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." So Blind CAN hear! I just can't see anything.

So I received Deaf's speech directly. Good - this confirms colors but I need wire safety info from the manual (Mute has that). Let me wait for Mute's input on which wire to cut.

```
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: No change on the board. Display 0, light yellow, wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute, if you can gesture instructions, I will pass along what I see.

I'm still waiting for Mute to provide manual information about which wire to cut. Mute reads the manual and can gesture to me (Blind) - but wait, I cannot see gestures! Mute's gesture only reaches Deaf and... let me check my own channels again.

Actually for MUTE's channels: Mute cannot speak, only gesture. "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it" - that was MY channel description. For Mute, gesturing would reach whoever can see - that's Deaf. I (Blind) cannot receive gestures at all per "You never receive gesture."

So Mute can only communicate to Deaf via gesture, and Deaf can then relay via speech to me (since I can hear). This matches what's happening - Deaf is asking Mute to gesture info, which Deaf will then verbally relay to me.

I need to wait for this relay to happen.

```
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Board unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. Mute, I see your gestures but have no key yet. Blind, stand by, no action confirmed.

We're stuck in a loop - Mute is gesturing but Deaf has no key to interpret the symbols meaningfully yet, or Mute hasn't sent gestures with clear meaning. I need to prompt Mute directly since Mute can hear me (I speak, Mute receives it).

Let me try to get things moving by speaking to Mute directly, asking them to establish a coding scheme with Deaf, or to relay instructions through gestures that Deaf can describe back to me in a way that maps to wire positions.

Since Mute reads the manual and knows which wire is safe, Mute needs to gesture that to Deaf using the alphabet, and Deaf needs to describe those exact symbols back to me so I can act. Let me ask Mute to establish a clear numeric gesture code (e.g., number of fingers = wire number) so Deaf can unambiguously relay it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, please gesture the wire number to cut using a single symbol like one finger for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3. Deaf will describe your exact gesture to me in words and I will act on it.")
```

Progress is being made in establishing a code between Mute and Deaf. I still need Deaf to explicitly tell me a number once the code is confirmed. Deaf says "two confirmed" - this suggests Mute gestured "2" as the wire number. But Deaf wants confirmation of the action (cut vs not cut) before relaying to me. Let me wait for that confirmation, since acting prematurely on incomplete info is risky.
